title: ANZ Frequent Flyer Black: 50,000 QFF Points with $6,000 Spend in 3 Months + 50,000 After 12 Months, $425 Annual Fee @ ANZ
body:
Deal: ANZ Frequent Flyer Black: 50,000 QFF Points with $6,000 Spend in 3 Months + 50,000 After 12 Months, $425 Annual Fee @ ANZ

[CodeXD] Another disappointing offer
Sad truths are sad
[Truck-kun] Luckily managed to get in right before they halved the bonus and removed the cashback. But it's disheartening to see these changes. Thanks albo
[OldSchoolHarry] The application process with ANZ was so frustrating that I had to withdraw my application last month.
[BatmanAU] Totally agree, with someone who had ANZ shares, big savings account with ANZ, $200k owing on a $800k mortgage (with off set), i had to nearly give over a kidney only to be declined.
Sold my shares, took my savings and moved my mortgage.
[OldSchoolHarry] I wasn't even declined, they just kept asking for more and more payslips and bank statements like last one year. I do a normal job that should easily meet the requirements.
[Truck-kun] Yup, I had to give them 1 whole year of payslip and 8-10 email correspondences and calls just to qualify… it's horrendous
[nightelves] You didn't have enough debt to warrant them looking at your application.
[littlesoldier] Used to be 160k qantas points, then 130k, 110k….. now 50k :(
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/691267
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/708551
[I like GoodDeals] From Memory, I think it used to be 150k Qantas points back in 2017 with $0 Annual fee..
Those were the good old days of Churning
[happydude] Depends how they are used.
https://freepoints.com.au/qantas-points-value/
[linkser] Only about 200-250 AUD in gift cards. But that's the worst possible way to spend the points.
If you use them for domestic reward flights, probably ~500 AUD if you get flights for low points. You can get more money/points if you book reward tickets for business class and international flights but you need also a lot more points for it and way harder to find the reward tickets.
[linkser] That is for domestic economy flights, value with Qantas is max. 1.5 cts/point I feel if one also considers the $40-50 still to pay in airport fees. You can get much better cts/point when looking for business class esp international.
[keji] They made the entire country worse off and changed a system that was already working. Makes me wonder who's at the wheel.
[VladImpaler] Most of the country couldn't care less about frequent-flyer points, but will be happy to be paying less for every single transaction.
I enjoyed buying lunch today and not having to do a mental calculation about how much it would cost to pay with either my Amex, Visa or Mastercard and whether the points were therefore good value.
[Xizor] Its hilarious you think the public will pay less as a result.
[VladImpaler] It's hilarious that people are pretending that no surcharge and reduced interchange fees will magically push prices up higher than what we paid for.
Much less the rubbish about businesses switching to cash and ignoring that then they'd have to make daily deposits at the 1 bank in the region.
[keji] @VladImpaler: ATO doesn't accept CC, can't deft my bills and poorer insurance coverage and introductory bonuses. If you think that we're charged less, think again.
If the idea is to save consumers money where exactly are we seeing the benefits when retail increases the price to absorb the charges.
[Drakesy] It's now getting built into the cost of everything.
[linkser] If the entire country would be cc churners, those points offers had stopped long along. I don't think its profitable to give a lot of customers FF points and then the customer just using the cc for the required amount and cancelling the card immediately.
Same for priv health. They do offer free weeks etc in the hope or knowledge most people then stick with them for years and pay premiums. Not for masses to get the free weeks and the next day move on to the next.
[Xizor] I think that is pretty obvious. Government spending and bloat has not radically increased in recent years by accident.
[ozmaxz] omg, it used to be 120k for the first year..now it cuts down less than a half..
[unison] It used to be 90K QFF with $5K spent before the most recent update.
[Buy2Much] ANZ is a waste of time. Had good income and good credit score (better than average). Not a credit card churner either. Applied twice in the last 5 years. After spending time filling application, sending them personal details, ID, all financial data, got rejected without giving any reason. Applied MyCard Premier, got it the first time without any hassle. Lower annual fee too.
[chk] makes sense since the changes to credit card surchanges came into effect today
[gamemaster] Another disappointing offer following the recent credit card surcharge changes.
It’s not a bargain. Why post offers which are not bargains? People shouldn’t be signing up for these substandard offers the banks are pushing. Banks will listen or reverse these greedy decisions if it costs them financially. Signing up for sub par offers only emboldens the banks to get away with their greed. No deal.
[GRP] I was a long time ANZ Black but churned. Some 4 o0r 5 years later I reapplied and will forever regret doing so as the anal queries on my financial status were just dumb (driven by Mumbai?) and I cancelled the application..
